brief: US 10y Treasury yields have risen over 100bp year-to-date and 130bp since the lows set on the eve of the US-Iran conflict, with front-end pricing hawkish versus GS's Fed baseline and 5y5y forwards 40-50bp above model fair value. GS attributes most of the move to a repricing of the Fed path from cuts to hikes, driven by rising inflation risk and reduced labor-market concern since the conflict's eve: higher policy-rate expectations alone explain about 70% of the YTD rise in 5y5y forwards, and a larger 80-85bp of the 10y yield move. A more optimistic growth outlook and bearish global spillovers add another 10-15bp combined. AI investment spending is also lifting yields through growth optimism, not through absorption of AI-related debt supply, which GS finds little evidence drives yields. About 10-15bp of the move is unexplained by the macro framework. Technical factors amplified the selloff: bond funds are now underweight duration to an extreme that has historically preceded lower yields over the next 1-2 quarters, and negative convexity in MBS/Treasury futures added selling pressure but should fade. GS turns more bullish on duration, recommending fading the cheapening by receiving 10s on the 5s10s30s fly.
